Vivek / Laura — looping you in to confirm what we should send. Key constraints from Akira:
- They want 31 Oct at 16:00 JST (please show "31 Oct 16:00 JST / 15:00 SGT" in the event title).
- Avoid sending an invite that only uses UTC; include explicit local-time strings in the description and title.
- Jin (SG) is fine with 15:00 SGT.

Vivek: can you confirm whether we should create three calendar events (one per local zone) or a single event with the primary timezone set to JST and an explicit line in the description for SGT/AEST? My worry: some users' clients (esp. older Exchange setups or regional calendar apps) convert only against the organizer's locale and may flip the date.

Suggested operational approach (my preference):
1) Create a primary invite with start time 31 Oct 16:00 JST (organizer timezone set to Asia/Tokyo).
2) Paste a text block in the description showing the corresponding local times for SGT and AEST and include the Zoom link and passcode.
3) Attach a separate ICS file labeled "invite-31oct-16-JST.ics" for recipients who want to import directly into their preferred calendar.

Laura — can you create the event and send both the calendar invite and the standalone ICS file as attachments? I’ll add a short sentence in the event title: "(31 Oct 16:00 JST / 15:00 SGT / 17:00 AEST)".

Thanks — Priya
